newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia needs $1.2bln-$2bln a year to develop-PM.
newsitem.headline: Serbia needs $1.2bln-$2bln a year to develop-PM.

text.p: Serbia needs up to $2 billion a year to develop but has problems in gathering foreign financial support while it remains outside key world financial bodies, Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic said.

"Experts estimate that Yugoslavia would need between $1.5 billion and $2 billion a year over the next several years to develop," Serbian Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic told Reuters in written answers to questions.

"Unfortunately, we must rely on our own resources but I am confident we shall successfully conclude reforms and structural adjustment of our banks and firms and enter the 21st century as an open, sophisticated European economy with dynamic economic growth and economic and social stability," Marjanovic said.

Marjanovic said that before nearly four years of U.N. sanctions "our economy was the most open one among East and Central European countries. Competition and market behaviour in Yugoslavia were at a much higher level than in other countries of the region."
Foreign funds were seen as vital to help Serbia conclude economic reforms and boost its idling industries.

"Market reforms would proceed much faster if they enjoyed support from world financial institutions and foreign investment," Marjanovic said and added it was difficult to forecast future investor attitude.
"Any answer assumes an anticipation of future behaviour of the international community toward our economy," he said.
Marjanovic insisted market reforms would attract more foreign interest.

"A healthy economic environment offered by an open market economy fostering competition would attract not only domestic investors but also woo foreign capital always in search for profitable projects and good business opportunities. Serbia and Yugoslavia offer such favourable conditions to everyone." -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
